results.summary_before: This project is a low-dropout (LDO) linear regulator implemented in an analog process, capable of supplying 0.1 to 4 mA at an output voltage of 1.4 to 1.8V. It consists of a BJT bandgap reference, two op-amps, and a pass PMOS transistor, with an external reference current set by a 90k resistor. The output voltage is available on ua[0], and testing requires a multimeter. The documentation is brief but provides the essential information for basic operation.

results.summary_before: Chasey is a maze game where the player controls a character to escape a ghost, rendered over VGA at 640x480 resolution. It uses five active-high buttons for reset and directional movement, and outputs VGA color and sync signals through a Tiny VGA PMOD. The design is implemented in SystemVerilog and runs on a 25 MHz clock. Silicon test results are not provided, so correct operation on hardware is not confirmed.

results.summary_before: The Environmental Mapping Processor is a small digital ASIC that averages and thresholds temperature, humidity and pressure samples and also computes whether a position is within a Manhattan distance of a target location. It takes sensor type, sample validity, output selection, clear and mode signals on the inputs, an 8-bit sensor data word on the bidirectional pins, and returns an 8-bit result plus status. The chip has no sensors or radio of its own; a portable implementation would pair it with a BME280, a GNSS receiver, a low-power microcontroller, a memory LCD, microSD storage and a LiPo battery. Reset and enable sequences are the only test guidance given, and the spatial grid is defined by the external controller.

results.summary_before: This mixed-signal chip integrates an 8-bit tracking analog-to-digital converter and an on-chip process variation monitor. The ADC uses analog pins for a reference voltage and input signal, while the process monitor outputs ring oscillator frequencies to assess fabrication variations. It is designed for analog and variation-sensing applications, with digital outputs for the ADC count and oscillator signals. The design is notable for combining these functions in a single Tiny Tapeout tile, but detailed usage and test procedures are not provided.
